problem: Spatial reasoning benchmarks test isolated QA and it is unknown whether spatial specialists or spatial supervision transfer to navigation; existing navigation methods apply spatial evidence uniformly without knowing which abilities matter at which phase or how spatial supervision should interact with decision learning.
motivation: Navigation needs continual use of spatial information over long horizons, unlike one-shot QA. The authors observe that benchmark-tuned spatial specialists underperform their base models in ObjectNav, while goal-coupled and phase-specific spatial supervision helps, motivating a training recipe built on these findings.
key_idea: Couple spatial supervision to the navigation goal, specialize it per navigation phase (Exploration vs Approach), and distill spatially-conditioned teacher action preferences into a student policy that acts without explicit spatial reasoning at inference.
insight: Spatial benchmark specialists (VST, ViLASR, Video-R1, SenseNova-SI) all fall below their base models in VLMNav/WMNav, while only navigation-coupled spatial annotations improve SR on both HM3D and VSI-Bench sources. Exploration benefits from Affordance/Topology and Approach from Visibility/Geometry, and serializing spatial text before the action removes the gain (59.4 vs 65.5 SR with parallel targets). Ablation of Spatial-NPD shows that shuffled priors give no gain (and hurt MP3D), so state-aligned priors are what matter; step-wise CoT costs 8.0/12.7 SR/SPL and 929 ms.
method: Spatial-Nav-100K: 112,886 supervision records built from ObjectNav rollouts on HM3D-v0.1/v0.2 train scenes; GPT-5.4 annotates Spatial Reasoning and Spatial2Nav Bridge (no action label) across 5 abilities (Visibility, Geometry, Relation, Topology, Affordance); exploration decisions are GPT-5.4 proposals filtered by simulator expert rules, and Approach STOP/CONTINUE labels come from a simulator distance check

Policy factorization: Approach policy chooses STOP/CONTINUE from RGB+goal; Exploration policy picks among depth-proposer candidate overlays; decision and spatial targets stored as separate sequences so action is never conditioned on generated spatial text
Stage 1 shared foundation: LoRA SFT of Qwen3-VL-8B on the weighted sum of decision NLL and spatial/bridge NLL (40K records)
Stage 2 phase experts: branch from the foundation; Exploration trained with Relation/Topology/Affordance and Approach with Visibility/Geometry/Relation, with a reweighted loss for the stop imbalance

Spatial-NPD: frozen teacher (same SFT branch) is given the aligned spatial annotation as extra input; the student sees only the navigation context; KL distillation over legal action logits (temperature 2) plus the direct decision loss; no spatial text at inference
Inference: Approach is called first, Exploration only on CONTINUE; 148 ms per decision at 1920x1080 and 110 ms at 512x288

setting.training_data: Spatial-Nav-100K (112,886 records from HM3D-v0.1/v0.2 train ObjectNav rollouts, GPT-5.4 annotated); ~45 A100 GPU-hours of policy training
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 1920x1080 plus goal category and candidate overlays from a fixed RGB-D depth-based proposer (policy sees RGB only)
setting.action_space: discrete candidate selection from depth-based proposer (each candidate a sequence of rotate/forward), plus STOP/CONTINUE
setting.privileged: none at test time (fixed onboard RGB-D proposer; spatial priors used only during training)

numbers.extra: 4-run mean; 500-step budget, 1.0 m success radius; 45 A100-hours training on Spatial-Nav-100K
4-run mean; trained on HM3D only, transferred directly

numbers_note: HM3D-v0.1/v0.2/MP3D splits are not labelled with official split names in the paper; 'val' is assumed. Headline results are four-seed means.
results: The 8B model reaches 77.4/35.4 SR/SPL on HM3D-v0.2, 60.2/30.5 on HM3D-v0.1 and 47.9/20.6 on MP3D, beating GPT-4o-based MSGNav (74.1/33.4 on v0.2) and Qwen-RobotNav (71.2/33.0) in SR, but not ApexNav (76.2/38.0 SPL) or Uni-Navid in SPL. Ablation goes from 59.2/22.1 (base) to 77.4/35.4 via SFT, phase experts, shared foundation, then NPD.
limitations: Only simulated ObjectNav with a fixed depth-based candidate proposer and controller; no real-robot, learned proposal or other tasks
Annotations, priors and exploration proposals all come from a single annotator (GPT-5.4), so its bias/noise may propagate
Navigation-coupled training does not improve all generic spatial benchmarks (OmniSpatial drops, VSI-Bench flat)
